chapter: Apollo Bar, Apollo managers and Harlem nightlife
title: Holdup at the Mummers Club
summary: He describes a tiny gunman holding up the Mummers Club on 33rd Street, and seeing the robbers partying at Small's, saying they were sending money to Sing Sing.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Another place I used to -- down to Mummer's Club, down on 33rd Street and one night, it was on a Saturday night and I was there and the place started fillingup and all these men come in and I said -- I don't know who it was, but I said so and so shouldn't let all these men in here, and I hadn't no more than said that then the cats jumped up on the table, little cat, he wasn't four feet and he had a great big pistol
and the bullets were pointing out the barrel, see, you could see them and he said this is a holdup. I said ain't this awful.

Yeah, they stuck the joint up and I had some tips in a bag and I eased it down and shoved it in my corner and they come to me and I said 'no, I ain't got nothing, ain't made nothing. It's been a bad night.' He said, 'yeah, we got to go up to Sing Sing with this money. We take up there to Sing Sing because they need some money.' So I went up to Small's that night and who do you suppose I saw them gangsters were up there.
They said they had to send money up to Sing Sing, and they robbed these places. Yeah, I had a colorful life.
You surely did, Tom. You deserve it.
